title: Audit stream connectors: backpressure, delivery semantics, and admin controls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define and implement a hardened audit-log delivery pipeline for external integrations (SIEMs, webhooks, Splunk HEC, Datadog, syslog) that provides clear delivery semantics, backpressure handling, admin controls, and RBAC enforcement. This ticket covers architecture, connector interface, retry/dedup strategies, DLQ behavior, and Console admin surfaces to configure guarantees and toggles.
acceptance_criteria: Documented delivery modes: at-least-once with idempotency keys, and at-most-once (best-effort) selectable per connector
Connector interface implemented for generic webhooks plus adapters for Splunk HEC and Datadog Logs API
Backpressure mechanism: internal buffering via Kafka topic + consumer-side concurrency limits and circuit-breaker when target returns 429/5xx
Dead-letter queue with alerting and manual replay UI in Console
RBAC v2 controls applied: only config-admin or security-admin roles can create/modify connectors; read-only roles can view status
Audit events include SSO identity telemetry (OIDC sub / SAML NameID) when available and respect PII redaction policy
Automated e2e integration tests (mock SIEM endpoints) exercise retries, jitter, DLQ and ordering guarantees
SLO defined and measurable: 99.5% of audit events accepted by downstream within 30s under steady-state
HMAC signing and TLS enforced for webhook payloads; Splunk/Datadog adapters support their recommended auth flows
tasks: Design connector API and schema versions (confluence: /wiki/audit-connectors-v2)
Implement generic webhook connector with HMAC signing and mTLS option
Adapter: Splunk HEC client with ack handling and batching
Adapter: Datadog Logs API client with rate-limit aware backoff
Integrate internal buffer (Kafka topic) and consumer worker pool with concurrency controls
DLQ implementation + Console replay UI mockup
RBAC enforcement hooks in Console and API endpoints
Add metrics and tracing (per-connector success/failure, latency, retry counts)
comments: 2026-02-10 Maya Chen: Kickoff - scoped to delivery guarantees and connectors. Initial idea: support two delivery modes (at-least-once + idempotent dedupe, and best-effort). Will require schema version in events and stable idempotency key generation (event_id + source). See draft design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/audit-connectors-v2/draft

2026-02-11 Diego Alvarez: Engineering notes - prefer using Kafka as the internal buffer to absorb spikes and provide stable retries. Workers will pull and apply per-connector backoff and circuit-breaker state. Sticky routing to worker instances to preserve ordering for tenant-scoped streams where required.

2026-02-12 Priya Singh (Security): Must ensure SSO/SAML identity fields are included when available; add redaction toggle controlled by customer and default PII-redaction rule. Also: require HMAC signing for webhooks and support mutual TLS for enterprise customers.

2026-02-13 Diego Alvarez: Decision log - delivery semantics: implement at-least-once by default with idempotency-key header (X-RW-Event-Id). Add opt-in at-most-once for customers that prefer lower latency. Replays from DLQ must preserve original event_id to avoid duplication on downstreams that are not idempotent.

2026-02-14 QA update - test matrix planned: healthy endpoint, transient 5xx with successful retry, persistent 4xx (e.g., 401/403), 429 rate-limit handling with Retry-After, long-tail storage spike and DLQ flow. Create mock endpoints in test harness (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-connector-mocks)

2026-02-15 Design feedback from Console PM (Anya Patel): Console should expose connector 'mode' (mode: at-least-once | best-effort), retry policy fields (max_attempts, base_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, jitter_pct), and a toggle for including identity metadata. Provide role-based visibility for secrets used by connectors.

2026-02-16 Infra note - retention of internal buffer topics aligned with customer contract; for Dedicated/Private deployments allow on-prem Kafka or in-cluster buffering. For hosted, default retention 48h before DLQing, configurable per-tenant.

2026-02-17 Diego Alvarez: Implementation progress - generic webhook connector PR opened (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-connectors/pull/198). Basic HMAC signing + retry loop implemented. Next: Splunk HEC adapter and DLQ wiring. Planning feature-flag toggle 'audit.connectors.v2' for staged rollout.
